item.title: Athletics Hire Taylor Smith As Next President of Baseball Operations
item.description: DETROIT, MI - JULY 08: A detailed view of a Wilson baseball glove and Athletics hat sitting in the Athletics dugout during the game against the Detroit Tigers at Comerica Park on July 8, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. The Tigers defeated the Athletics 6-1. (Photo by Mark Cunningham/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The wait for the next leader of the A’s is over. We have our guy. The organization has named Red Sox assistant General Manager Taylor Smith as the newest President of Baseball Operations, per a team announcement: Welcome to the Green & Gold, Taylor! We have named Taylor Smith as our President of Baseball Operations. pic.twitter.com/Y9FeEkwMxC — Athletics (@Athletics) October 19, 2026 The A’s had been connected to Smith for the past few weeks, with the team first interviewing Smith almost exactly a month ago. There’d been other names connected to the A’s job ( most notably Sam Fuld, who rejected the Athletics’ gig ) but Smith’s name continued to be brought up as a real possibility. Jon Heyman recently reported that the A’s were “focused on” Smith after getting rejected by Fuld, and now they have a deal in place for him to lead us into the next era of A’s baseball. Smith comes with fresh ideas but not a lot of experience. Still in his early 30’s (still waiting for exact confirmation on his age), he first began his baseball career with the Tampa Bay Rays, joining them as an analyst in their research and development department after graduating from the University of Georgia in in 2018. He spent the better part of the next half decade rising up their system. By the time the Red Sox poached him from their division rivals in 2024, he’s risen all the way to director of predictive marketing in Tampa. Over the past two years he’s been one of Boston POBO Craig Breslow’s lieutenants, in charge of their analytics department. What Smith lacks in experience, he should make up for with fresh ideas for an organization that hasn’t had an outside hire like this in decades. Smith now has a couple of weeks to get his sea legs under him and prepare for his first offseason running the Athletics. He’ll need to staff his front office (presumably with former Red Sox and Rays staffers) before deciding whether or not he wants to stick with incumbent manager Mark Kotsay. There’s been no indication one way or another but for what it’s worth Kotsay is signed through 2028. After all of that, Smith’s biggest challenge will begin: fixing the A’s pitching staff. The core of a playoff team is there on the position player side of things, but the pitching has been a major problem for the past two years and that has to be the immediate focus for Smith. Jury is still out on how the new ballpark in Las Vegas will play, but Smith has the ability to shape this team to how he sees fit. Let’s hope this is a home run hire!

item.title: NBA experts predict the New York Knicks will fall short in their championship defense
item.description: NBA experts predict the New York Knicks will fall short in their championship defense originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . When the New York Knicks went on a magical run in the 2026 Playoffs, people were surprised. They did not have the best regular season in the 2025-26 campaign, so people thought the Detroit Pistons or a recharged Boston Celtics would dominate the Eastern Conference side of the Playoffs. However, the Knicks pulled off the surprise run, as they looked like the best team in the league until they beat the San Antonio Spurs in five games in the NBA Finals to win their first title in 52 seasons. Now, that has set expectations for the 2026-27 season. The Knicks are not considered favorites by ESPN's experts Ahead of the 2026-27 season, a lot of people still have the Knicks winning the championship. They would become the first team in nearly a decade to repeat as champions, as the Golden State Warriors last did it in 2017 and 2018. Unfortunately, they will face some stiff competition from the East's recharged teams like the Philadelphia 76ers and the Miami Heat . However, the experts at ESPN are in agreement that a Western Conference team will take the title this year. MORE: Knicks head coach Mike Brown speaks on what he is looking forward to in the 2026-27 season Both the Spurs and the Oklahoma City Thunder are seen as the favorites to win the championship. Not one person from ESPN's 15-person team of experts has picked the Knicks . In that group, 10 people picked the Shai Gilgeous-Alexander-led Thunder , while the other five believe the Spurs will get their redemption a year later from their loss in the Finals. From the same 15-person panel, only five people agree that the Knicks will get back to the Finals. The 76ers got the same number of votes, while the rest of the votes went to the Celtics , Indiana Pacers , and the Toronto Raptors . item.description: Deone Walker is probably going to be the antagonist in Tyler Linderbaum’s nightmares for a while. The Raiders made Linderbaum the NFL’s highest-paid center this offseason, inking him to a three-year, $81 million deal with $60M guaranteed at signing, and the Bills disruptive nose tackle demolished him for a large portion of Buffalo’s 33-30 win over Las Vegas in Week 6. Now, Walker was only credited with one pressure on 30 pass-rush snaps, but he “won” his one-on-one reps with Linderbaum far more frequently than that, and he wreaked havoc against the Raiders run game, a ground attack that only averaged 3.3 yards per rush. Linderbaum had become an elite-level center during his time in Baltimore, before he signed the monster free-agent deal in Las Vegas. He routinely won with a tremendous combination of balance, agility, and power. Remember too, Linderbaum was an All-State wrestler in high school who famously pinned Tristan Wirfs back in a 2017 match between the future NFL offensive linemen. Walker tossed the 6’2”, 305-pound Linderbaum aside like he was a practice-squad long-snapper on that rep then wrapped up Mike Washington for a short gain. All-Pro level highlight there. At Iowa and early in his career with the Ravens, Linderbaum was a menace in the run game because of how rapidly he erupted out of his stance when either climbing the second level or getting to reach blocks across a gap. item.title: Marcus Caldeira completes Minnesota's rally | Energy Moment of the Matchday
item.description: Marcus Caldeira completes Minnesota's rally | Energy Moment of the Matchday By Jaime Uribarri Energy Moment of the Matchday 31: Marcus Caldeira Did Marcus Caldeira score the goal of the season for Minnesota United FC ? The Canadian international striker completed a miracle 3-2 comeback win against St. Louis CITY SC on Saturday, netting the dramatic game-winner at Allianz Field that also earned him Energy Moment of the Matchday presented by Celsius honors for Matchday 31. Down two goals at home against the league's hottest team, the Loons fought back with three unanswered goals from Aziel Jackson , Kelvin Yeboah and Caldeira, the latter finishing off an epic breakaway in the 86th minute. The miracle win halted St. Louis CITY's unbeaten league streak at 19 games, one shy of setting a new MLS record. It also gave Minnesota their first home win since April and a glimmer of hope in making the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs. With four regular-season games remaining, the Loons have 34 points – five back of the Western Conference's ninth and final playoff spot. Caldeira and the Loons continue their late-season push on Saturday at Houston Dynamo FC (8:30 pm ET | Apple TV ).

item.title: Atlético and Nike open final vote for Manto da Massa 2026/27
item.description: Atlético and Nike open final vote for Manto da Massa 2026/27 After announcing their partnership under the slogan “The Greatest Play Together” and launching this season’s kits, Atlético and Nike are unveiling the three finalist shirts competing to become the official Manto da Massa for 2026/27. For the first time, the designs were developed collaboratively, taking fans’ preferences into account and expanding their role in the creative process. “The Fans” was the chosen theme, highlighting the central role of those who make Galo what it is. An assist against Elche, his first goal against Villarreal, another assist against Roma, and most recently, a stunning goal against Sevilla – the former RBL winger is starting to find his feet at Real Madrid . Since leaving RB Leipzig last summer, the Ivorian has been getting more and more playing time for Los Blancos, increasing the chances of him coming up against his former club on Wednesday evening (21:00 CEST). Mourinho giving Yan time to develop Yan also needed some time to settle in at Real Madrid. With new teammates, unfamiliar surroundings and high expectations to contend with, José Mourinho was keen to ease the youngster into the side. “ There’s no need to rush. He has to take things one step at a time,” Mourinho explained after the opening weeks of the season. “He’s training well and working hard. He’s open-minded and keeps his feet on the ground. He wants to learn, he wants to work. He listens to me and to his teammates, and he’ll continue to improve.” Mourinho also pointed out that Yan had only one season of experience at the highest level of club football under his belt before moving to Madrid. item.content:encoded: Jesse Johnson-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0 coming out of their bye week, and The Athletic’s Alec Lewis already told us he expects the front office to be “really, really active” before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. On Monday morning, Lewis went a step further and laid out five positions the Vikings could look to upgrade. Safety was the least likely of the five, by his own admission. However, that’s only if you are thinking short-term. Of the five positions here, safety might be the most far-fetched given its complexity in Flores’ system. Mastering the communication on the back end requires hundreds of training camp reps. Without them, it would be tough to expect major production… Alec Lewis – The Athletic Because long term, with 37-year-old Harrison Smith in his final season and no succession plan in place behind him, this team has no safety of the future to hand the secondary to. That makes both of the safety names listed intriguing. However, there’s only one that will catch the eye of Gopher fans too. Could Vikings get another shot at Antoine Winfield Jr.? In the 2020 NFL Draft, the MN Vikings passed on Antoine Winfield Jr. multiple times before he was eventually selected in the second round (45th overall) by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Despite then-Vikings general manager Rick Spielman watching the Minnesota Gophers legend ball out in person for years during his college career in Dinkytown, he and former head coach Mike Zimmer selected CB Jeff Gladney with the No. 31 overall pick, instead of “reaching” for Winfield Jr. Related: Winfield Jr Says Vikings Didn’t Have Much Interest in Drafting Him Gladney struggled as a rookie , recording just 3 passes defended in 15 starts, then tragically passed away in May 2022. Winfield, 28, has accumulated 561 tackles, 18 sacks, 9 interceptions and 12 forced fumbles in 89 NFL starts (all with TB). He’s also made two Pro Bowls and one first-team All-Pro nod (2023). He also helped Tampa win a Super Bowl his rookie year. Antoine Winfield Jr. balled out in the Super Bowl as a rookie! @AntoineWJr11 | #SBLV https://t.co/5WCKVLWsFS — NFL (@NFL) February 13, 2021 And now, two general managers later, Nolan Teasley could be staring at the perfect opportunity to right a wrong of his predecessor’s predecessor, before the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline. Alec Lewis floats MN Gopher legend as MN Vikings trade target As I mentioned above, Alec’s article Monday at The Athletic listed safety as the Minnesota Vikings’ fifth and final position to watch for a possible trade, going as far as to call it “the most far-fetched” of the five. Unless, of course, Teasley can get his hands on a real gamechanger, not just for the rest of 2026, but into the future as well. Specifically, Lewis names Budda Baker and Antoine Winfield Jr. as the two safety targets where “taking a swing will be worth a conversation.” Taking a swing will be worth a conversation if players such as Antoine Winfield Jr. or Budda Baker are available. The Vikings would also be smart to think about a contingency plan for Smith in the form of an elite player with blitzing savvy and presnap deciphering chops. Alec Lewis – The Athletic Why Antoine Winfield Jr. trade makes sense for Vikings right now Winfield signed a four-year, $84.1 million extension with Tampa Bay on May 13, 2024, which included $45 million fully guaranteed, all of which has already been paid out. Both 2026 and 2027 ($19.6M) are non-guaranteed. He’s owed $19.5 million this season, and roughly half of that would still be left by the Nov. 10 deadline, meaning the Minnesota Vikings could trade for Winfield, with the plan to extend and lock him in as safety of the future this offseason. The Vikings already have Josh Metellus under contract through 2028, after his three-year, $36 million extension in 2025. Adding the 28-year-old Winfield next to him would fix the Vikings’ future at safety before they even get to the offseason, leaving one less task on Teasley’s lengthy to-do list next spring/summer. What would the Minnesota Vikings have to give up to get Winfield Jr.? Well, his market may be more suppressed now than any other time during his career, meaning it’s the perfect time to strike. Down year in Tampa Bay? Through four games , the former Gopher has just 24 tackles with zero forced fumbles, zero interceptions, zero passes defended and zero sacks. Five of those tackles came in the Vikings’ 23-16 win in Tampa back in Week 3. He’s also been banged up lately. Winfield fractured a rib in the Bucs’ 17-14 loss to the Packers on Oct. 4 and has missed games against Dallas and Pittsburgh since. On Friday, Bucs reporter Greg Auman saw him working on the side with a trainer. Winfield was working on the side with a trainer today. First I’ve seen him since his injury. Hard to know whether next week would be in play for him or not. — Greg Auman (@gregauman) October 16, 2026 Related: Insiders Clash on Vikings’ Trade Plans for Disgruntled Wide Receiver With the Bucs sitting at 1-5, Tampa Bay media has taken notice and multiple outlets are calling for the Bucs to trade Winfield Jr., while he still holds some value. Scott Reynolds ( Pewter Report ) named Winfield one of the Bucs’ “three logical candidates” to trade, writing that he “hasn’t come close to living up to his $21 million per year salary.” Others have suggested much of the same, though no insiders have reported any actual trade steam out of Florida just yet. Antoine Winfield Jr. is a MN legend, but so is his dad… Before he was a Buccaneer, Antoine Winfield Jr. was one of the best players to ever wear maroon and gold and play home football games in Dinkytown. In 2019, his final collegiate season, the Minnesota star was named a unanimous All-American , just the seventh in school history and the first since Greg Eslinger in 2005. Antoine Winfield Jr. from @GopherFootball was a unanimous All-American and is now up for Golden Goldys Men’s Athlete of the Year! Take a look at some of his highlights here! #Gophers. https://t.co/tP6Qg06wbS — The Gopher Way (@thegopherway) April 18, 2020 Related: What We Learned from Another Ugly MN Vikings Victory in Week 3 That same season, he was crowned Big Ten Defensive Back of the Year and named a finalist for the Bronko Nagurski Award. His seven interceptions tied the Gophers’ all-time single-season record. It’s also worth noting that the Minnesota Vikings acquired Winfield Jr.’s father around this same time of his career. In the 2004 offseason, the 26-year-old Antoine Winfield Sr. signed with the Vikings in free agency as a budding defensive back in the league. All Winfield Sr. did after signing in Minnesota was stay here 9 seasons, play in three Pro Bowls and become one of the best corners in franchise history. Read more at Minnesota Sports Fan

item.title: Shane Steichen has zero issues with Colts fans booing as insider warns firings are coming
item.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images Shane Steichen has zero issues with Colts fans booing as insider warns firings are coming appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indianapolis Colts suffered one of their worst losses in recent memory on Sunday. Indy lost 26-20 against Tennessee , giving their division rival their first win of the 2026 season. The panic level has jumped up a few levels in Indy after losing to one of the NFL’s worst teams in a must-win situation. Colts head coach Shane Steichen explained why he doesn’t care about fans booing after Sunday’s disastrous loss. “We gotta give them something to cheer about. You know? I don’t blame them for booing one freakin’ bit,” Steichen told reporters after the game on Sunday per Ari Meirov. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) QB Daniel Jones did not play well against the Titans. He finished 22-of-42 for 269 passing yards with one touchdown and two interceptions. Jones also added three carries for 30 rushing yards. The Colts have been hamstrung for nearly the entire 2026 season. Top receiver Alec Pierce has only played in two games because of heel and ankle injuries. Indy was also without tight end Tyler Warren on Sunday, which spread the offensive talent incredibly thin. Indy is now in danger of unraveling completely after falling to 2-4 on the season. And the latest reports from one Colts insider make the situation look especially fraught. The Athletic’s James Boyd warned that job losses for the team brass now seem like an inevitability. “Worst loss of the Shane Steichen era and one of the worst losses of Chris Ballard’s tenure as well,” Boyd wrote on social media. “Nothing anyone says would be hyperbolic. This team is terrible. Everyone should be embarrassed. Jobs being lost feels like a matter of when not if.” The Colts need to start stringing some wins together in a hurry. If they cannot stem the bleeding, the entire Steichen era could be coming to an end very soon. Unfortunately, Indy faces another tough task next week. Next up for the Colts is a road game against the undefeated Vikings in Week 7. Related: Is Shane Steichen joining Colts GM Chris Ballard out the door after Titans embarrassment? Related: It’s time for Colts to bench Daniel Jones, give Anthony Richardson another chance after losing to Titans

item.title: 49ers insider hints at Vita Vea trade desires after Buccaneers blow game vs. Steelers
item.description: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images 49ers insider hints at Vita Vea trade desires after Buccaneers blow game vs. Steelers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Francisco 49ers will be facing the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football as they try to extend their undefeated streak. They’re one of the best teams in the league, and it wouldn’t be a surprise if they got even better over the coming weeks. That could be because of getting players back from injury, or simply making a trade to improve their roster. 49ers insider David Lombardi is already throwing hits out about the latter, and after the Tampa Bay Buccaneers fell to 1-5 after their loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, he hinted at a specific player , which was Vita Vea . 👀 pic.twitter.com/oKVpSYheG7 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — David Lombardi (@LombardiHimself) October 18, 2026 This doesn’t mean that the 49ers are interested in him, but they could definitely use a player of his caliber on the defensive line. Vea and the Buccaneers weren’t on the same page before the start of the season, but they were able to give him a contract extension. Now, with the Buccaneers’ season looking the way it is, it would be in their best interest to at least try to trade some players for picks. Vea could get them something good, but they also might want to stand pat and see if they can revive their season when Baker Mayfield gets back. As for the 49ers, if they believe they need one or two pieces to truly feel like contenders, they may offer whatever they have. The defense has dealt with some injuries, so adding someone to the defensive line or secondary could be their top priorities. Of course, with any possible trade, another team has to be willing to give up a player or any other asset. It’ll be interesting to see if the 49ers actually go after a player like Vea, or if Lombardi’s picture was just a pipe dream at the moment. item.title: Greatness is the standard for UCLA's Bob Chesney
item.description: Greatness is the standard for UCLA's Bob Chesney originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The UCLA Bruins have turned heads this season. They are the only undefeated team left in the Big Ten, and head coach Bob Chesney expected nothing less from his squad. UCLA sits atop the Big Ten standings (6-0, 4-0). They come off a 17-7 win over Wisconsin on Saturday and have been picking teams off one by one. Concerns remain about the offense without Nico Iamaleava out for the season, but they won their first game without him. "We never put like limits on what we did or could not do. And we also didn't make excuses. Like, hey, let's just get bowl eligible; that was never a thing either. That's an excuse for why you might have success," Chesney said in his post-game press conference. Bob Chesney reacts to UCLA being the last undefeated team standing across the Big Ten and SEC https://t.co/F84m05FH97 — FOX College Football (@CFBONFOX) October 18, 2026 "Not really major expectations in my mind; we were going to go about this the way you have to go about this." Backup quarterback Ty Dieffenbach stepped up in a huge way for UCLA. He completed 22-of-33 passes for 264 passing yards and an interception. He threw his only interception on a Hail Mary at the end of the first half. Dieffenbach looked as if he had been there before. The Bruins' defense has looked much more physical this season, and their record reflects that. Chesney was hired in December 2025 and has already led the Bruins to their best start since 2022. The Bruins finished 3-9 in their 2025 campaign. item.title: 14 things you forgot happened in the NBA offseason, from Giannis and Jaylen Brown trades to Clippers' punishment
item.description: 14 things you forgot happened in the NBA offseason, from Giannis and Jaylen Brown trades to Clippers' punishment originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Chances are, if you're an NBA fan, you've heard about LeBron James' new team. James' move to the 76ers was the headliner of a busy NBA offseason, with the league's all-time leading scorer departing the Lakers on a veteran's minimum contract to form an elite starting five in Philadelphia. But even outside of James, it's been a long summer full of moves — since the Knicks were crowned champions in June, a collection of stars have changed teams, new coaches were hired, and major changes were announced for multiple franchises. Here are 14 signings, trades, hires, and more you may have forgotten about from the past NBA offseason. MORE: The Sporting News' NBA preseason power rankings 14 things you forgot happened in the NBA offseason David Kirouac - IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Giannis Antetokounmpo traded to Heat It may feel like Giannis Antetokounmpo has been a member of the Heat for a while, considering all of the news that has unfolded since then. But in early June, Antetokounmpo talks were dragging out more than ever. After months-worth of speculation about whether or not the Bucks would move on, once they made real indications that they'd be trading their franchise star, two teams emerged as the favorite to land Antetokounmpo: the Celtics and Heat. Boston was reportedly dangling Jaylen Brown in Antetokounmpo talks, but ultimately, Miami won the bidding war by sending Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparash Jakcionis, the No. 13 pick, a 2030 first-round pick swap, unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033 and a 2033 second-round pick to Milwaukee. In the deal first reported on June 22, Antetokounmpo changed teams for the first time in his NBA career, and he now forms an elite big man duo with Bam Adebayo in South Beach. MORE: Grading the Giannis Antetokounmpo Bucks-Heat blockbuster Big-name rookies find new homes There was a lot of hype surrounding the 2026 NBA rookie class thanks to a "Big Four" of sorts. But even outside of James, it's been a long summer full of moves — since the Knicks were crowned champions in June, a collection of stars have changed teams, new coaches were hired, and major changes were announced for multiple franchises. item.title: Tyler Loop breaks down Browns game-ruining missed FG that aided another double-digit blown lead
item.description: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Tyler Loop breaks down Browns game-ruining missed FG that aided another double-digit blown lead appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Baltimore Ravens were dealt another brutal loss, this time to the Cleveland Browns. The Ravens pulled off a huge overtime win over the Atlanta Falcons last Sunday, even without Lamar Jackson, but they gave up a double-digit lead. That was partly because Tyler Loop missed a crucial 4th-quarter field goal. Early in the fourth quarter, Loop missed a 49-yard field goal that would have put the Ravens up 13-3. When the Ravens got the ball back, Derrick Henry fumbled, giving the Browns the ball on the Baltimore 35-yard line and ultimately scoring touchdowns that secured the lead. In a quote obtained by Jamison Hensley, Loop discussed his missed field goal that ultimately cost the team the game. In a quote obtained by Jamison Hensley, Loop discussed his missed field goal that ultimately cost the team the game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I just did not strike it the way I needed to. Didn’t hit the ball clean and ended up having some bad rotation and just sliding out to the left,” he said. The loss is the Ravens’ 17th double-digit blown lead since the 2018 season, the most in the NFL. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter spoke about Henry’s fumble in post-game media availability, defending the star running back. “Nobody works harder at ball security [than Henry]. It happened, [and] it was a good play by them. I’d like for us to be able to rise up and get a stop right there and have each other’s backs, [and] we weren’t able to do that. It becomes an even bigger play when you’re not able to kind of back it up with the defense. So, it is what it is.” The Ravens play the Bengals on Sunday. item.title: Allegri: ‘I question myself every day, Napoli players must be defended’
item.description: Allegri: ‘I question myself every day, Napoli players must be defended’ Massimiliano Allegri has warned Napoli about Bodø/Glimt’s danger on the break as the pressure builds ahead of Tuesday’s Champions League clash at the Maradona. According to the Corriere dello Sport , Allegri said at his pre-match press conference that Napoli are still searching for their first points after losing at home to Arsenal and 3-1 at Villarreal. “The game will be complicated, regardless of the other results,” he said. “Last year Bodø/Glimt had a good Champions League, and they’re good on the counter-attack.” “They’re a strong side, very quick. In Munich, despite the result, they played a good game. They’re dangerous when they win the ball back, so it will take a big performance.” The Norwegians beat Borussia Dortmund 1-0 last time out. VENICE, ITALY – OCTOBER 17: Akor Adams of Venezia FC competes for the ball with Sam Beukema of SSC Napoli during the Serie A match between Venezia FC and SSC Napoli at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo on October 17, 2026 in Venice, Italy. (Photo by Maurizio Lagana/Getty Images) Allegri defends Napoli players amid criticism Saturday’s 1-0 defeat at Venezia , where Kevin De Bruyne had a penalty saved, left Napoli with five losses in nine games in all competitions. It is the first time that has happened to them in 25 years. “Only we can get ourselves out of this,” Allegri insisted. “If we manage to win tomorrow, we’ll see things differently.” “You have to question yourself every day. I’ve always done that, and I’ll keep doing it as long as I enjoy this job.” NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 10: Massimiliano Allegri, Manager of SSC Napoli, gestures during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Frosinone Calcio at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 10, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) The coach then hit back at the criticism of his squad. “I’m sorry the players have been criticised in a certain way,” he said. “Players must be defended and helped, even in difficult moments. They all have my unconditional trust. But when things are difficult, they mustn’t be thrown overboard. They have to lift their heads and show they’re worthy of Napoli.” Allegri also hinted at more rotation, with Napoli facing a packed schedule. “We have nine games in a month and another nine after the second international break. We can’t always play the same XI. Everyone can play for us.”

item.title: The NBA Is Aggressively Integrating Artificial Intelligence Across Several Facets of Its Operations
item.description: Image: Sony Missed out-of-bounds calls, betting scandals tied to player-performance props, and stars who reshape possessions without touching the ball yet vanish from the box score: the NBA is treating all three as problems technology can help solve. The league is deploying artificial intelligence across three distinct fronts: officiating accuracy, competitive integrity surveillance, and performance analytics. Sony Hawk-Eye , a sensor-embedded Wilson basketball , and Amazon Web Services form the core of that effort, and what they do affects the game you watch. Calling It Right: The Smart Ball and What It Changes Optical tracking and an embedded sensor could automate the objective calls that currently send games to lengthy replay review. Sony’s Hawk-Eye system captures player and ball movement in three dimensions with very low latency, according to an NBA partnership announcement. It supports advanced analytics and is designed to eventually automate objective decisions such as out-of-bounds rulings and goaltending calls. item.title: At Strasbourg, Gio Reyna is starting to gain what had been elusive: momentum
item.description: A goal against PSG is proof on the scoresheet of what can be seen on the teamsheet: at long last, Reyna is getting consistent minutes For an entire four-year cycle, to write about Gio Reyna was to write about his potential – especially the nagging feeling that it was going unfulfilled. Once hyped as possibly the greatest prospect in US men’s history, a series of injuries kept him from simply taking the field, much less making his mark on it. Since his emergent 2020-21 season, when he logged nearly 2,000 Bundesliga minutes running alongside Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham, and Jadon Sancho, Reyna finished each of the ensuing five seasons without even cresting 630 league minutes. “Rotational” became a generous descriptor for his role at Nottingham Forest on loan, and then last season with Borussia Mönchengladbach. Still, Gregg Berhalter and Mauricio Pochettino kept involving Reyna with the US squad based on that pesky potential – betting that, on his day, he still had the raw talent to do what few compatriots could. item.title: Another unremarkable win shows Arsenal’s strength is in depth rather than creativity | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Champions so risk-averse Forest were lured into thinking they had a chance, until bench was used to see them off Pass. Pass. Pass. Pass. Sideways. Square. Backwards. Pass. Pass. Recycle. Pass. It wasn’t much of a spectacle. But in the end, for the second week running, thanks in no small part of their bench, Arsenal won. Fireworks in the autumn are for Bonfire Night; titles require relentless accumulation. Since the international break, Arsenal have won three games out of three despite not being in the lead at half-time in any of them. Hammered at Brighton and having endured a drab first hour at home to Leeds last week, there has been a rare sense, for the first time really since Manchester City dropped points at Everton at the beginning of May, of Arsenal not being quite at their best, needing to reassert their quality. This was not a performance that would terrify any opponent, but it did highlight Arsenal’s consistency and it did demonstrate just how deep their squad now runs. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.description: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied Usually, the second weekend of October sees Christian Pulisic flanked by compatriots as the Star-Spangled Banner plays. item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
